from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Initial position of electron above nucleus
        base_pos = nucleus.get_center()

        # Spring definition (8 segments)
        def get_spring_points(start, end):
            vec = end - start
            length = np.linalg.norm(vec)
            if length < 0.1: return [start, end]
            unit = vec / length
            perp = np.array([-unit[1], unit[0], 0]) * 0.2
            pts = [start]
            for i in range(1, 8):
                side = 1 if i % 2 == 1 else -1
                pts.append(start + (i/8)*vec + side*perp)
            pts.append(end)
            return pts

        spring = VMobject().set_stroke(color="#AAAAAA", width=3)
        spring.set_points_as_corners(get_spring_points(nucleus.get_center(), electron.get_center()))

        # Updaters for Line 1 oscillation

            # Slow natural oscillation
            offset = 1.5 + 0.2 * np.sin(time_tracker.get_value() * 3)
            mob.move_to(base_pos + UP * offset)

            mob.set_points_as_corners(get_spring_points(nucleus.get_center(), electron.get_center()))

        # Transition to row of atoms
        self.play(
            FadeOut(atom_bg), FadeOut(nucleus), FadeOut(electron), FadeOut(spring),
            FadeOut(e_field_arrow), FadeOut(e_field_label)
        )
        
        electron.remove_updater(update_electron_line2)
        spring.remove_updater(update_spring)
        
        # Row of 5 atoms
        atoms = VGroup()
        nuclei = VGroup()
        electrons = VGroup()
        springs = VGroup()
        
        grid_cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]
        for col_idx in grid_cols:
            a = SVGMobject(atom_path).set_color(DARK_GREY).set_opacity(0.2).scale(0.4)
            self.place_at_grid(a, f"D{col_idx}")
            n = SVGMobject(nucleus_path).set_color("#FF0000").scale(0.1).move_to(a.get_center())
            e = Dot(color="#0000FF", radius=0.08).move_to(n.get_center() + UP * 0.6)
            s = VMobject().set_stroke(color="#AAAAAA", width=2)
            s.set_points_as_corners(get_spring_points(n.get_center(), e.get_center()))
            
            atoms.add(a)
            nuclei.add(n)
            electrons.add(e)
            springs.add(s)

        # Light wave
        wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.6 * np.sin(2 * PI * (x - 0.5) / 2.2),
            x_range=[0.5, 6.0],
            color=WHITE
        )
        wave.shift(RIGHT * 0.5 + DOWN * 0.2) # Centering roughly with row D

        def update_wave(mob):
            phase = time_tracker.get_value() * 4
            mob.become(
                FunctionGraph(
                    lambda x: 0.6 * np.sin(2 * PI * (x - 0.5) / 2.2 - phase),
                    x_range=[0.5, 6.0],
                    color=WHITE
                ).shift(DOWN * 0.8) # Row D height is approx -0.8
            )

        def update_row_electrons(mob_group):
            phase = time_tracker.get_value() * 4
            for i, e_dot in enumerate(mob_group):
                grid_x = self.grid[f"D{grid_cols[i]}"][0]
                # Match wave phase at that x
                val = 0.6 * np.sin(2 * PI * (grid_x - 0.5) / 2.2 - phase)
                base_y = self.grid[f"D{grid_cols[i]}"][1]
                e_dot.move_to([grid_x, base_y + 0.6 + val, 0])
                
                # Update corresponding spring
                springs[i].set_points_as_corners(
                    get_spring_points(nuclei[i].get_center(), e_dot.get_center())
                )

        self.play(FadeIn(atoms), FadeIn(nuclei), FadeIn(electrons), Create(springs))
        self.play(Create(wave))
        
        electrons.add_updater(update_row_electrons)
        wave.add_updater(update_wave)
        
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(10), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        self.place_at_grid(electron, 'C3', scale_factor=0.5)

        electron.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.shift(UP * 0.1 * np.sin(self.internal_time * 10) * dt * 10))
        self.add(electron)

        circles = VGroup()
        def create_expanding_circle():
            c = Circle(radius=0.1, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2)
            c.move_to(electron.get_center())
            return c

        def update_circles(obj, dt):
            self.internal_time += dt
            for c in obj:
                c.scale(1 + 2 * dt)
                c.set_stroke(opacity=max(0, 1 - c.get_radius() / 3))
            
            # Periodically add a new circle
            if int(self.internal_time * 5) > int((self.internal_time - dt) * 5):
                obj.add(create_expanding_circle())
            
            # Remove old circles (using list to safely remove during iteration)
            for c in list(obj):
                if c.get_radius() > 3:
                    obj.remove(c)

        circles.add_updater(update_circles)
        self.add(circles)

outline.topic: The Microscopic Origin and Dispersion of the Index of Refraction
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate Physics/Optics Students or Advanced High School Physics Students

sections.title: The Macroscopic Mystery
sections.content: Introduction to the concept that light slows down in media. Define the refractive index (n) as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum (c) to the phase velocity in the medium (v). Pose the fundamental question: Since light doesn't actually 'hit' particles like a ball, why does the speed change?
sections.example: A 'Lifeguard' analogy: To reach a person in the water, a lifeguard runs fast on sand but swims slower in water, changing their path to minimize time—just like light 'choosing' the path of least time (Fermat's Principle).

sections.title: Prerequisite: Atoms as Oscillators
sections.content: Introduce the Lorentz Oscillator Model. Explain that electrons are bound to nuclei like 'masses on springs.' Light is an electromagnetic wave with an oscillating electric field that exerts a force on these electrons, causing them to vibrate at the frequency of the incoming light.
sections.example: Visualizing a row of atoms as tiny weights attached to springs. When an external 'invisible hand' (the light wave) pushes them, they begin to bob up and down rhythmically.

sections.title: The Origin: Wave Superposition
sections.content: The microscopic origin is not absorption and re-emission, but wave interference. The oscillating electrons emit their own secondary electromagnetic waves. These secondary waves are slightly 'out of phase' with the original wave. When you sum the original wave and the secondary waves (Superposition), the resulting 'net' wave has a shifted phase, which appears as a slower velocity.
sections.example: Animation of a main wave passing through a crowd. Each person (atom) waves their hands slightly late, creating a 'ripple' that lags behind the main movement, effectively slowing the 'pulse' of the crowd.

sections.title: Color Dependence: The Resonance Factor
sections.content: Explain why the refractive index (n) changes with color (frequency). Electrons have a 'natural resonance frequency' (usually in the UV range). As the frequency of light (color) gets closer to this resonance, the interaction becomes stronger. Blue light (higher frequency) is closer to the UV resonance than red light (lower frequency), causing a greater phase shift and a higher refractive index.
sections.example: A playground swing: If you push the swing at a frequency close to its natural rhythm, you get a much larger and more 'lagged' response than if you push it very slowly.

sections.title: Visualizing the Math: Cauchy’s Equation
sections.content: Introduce the mathematical relationship between wavelength (λ) and refractive index (n). Use Cauchy's Equation: n(λ) = A + B/λ². Instead of just symbols, use a dynamic graph where the Y-axis is 'Slowness' (n) and the X-axis is 'Wavelength' (λ). Show the curve dropping as λ increases.
sections.example: On the graph, place a 'Red Apple' icon at the long-wavelength end (low n) and a 'Violet Grape' icon at the short-wavelength end (high n) to visually demonstrate why violet light bends more.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Rainbow Effect
sections.content: Conclude by applying the concepts to dispersion. Because n is different for each color, a prism refracts each color at a different angle. This explains why white light splits into a spectrum and how raindrops create rainbows.
sections.example: A visual breakdown of a camera lens 'Chromatic Aberration.' Show how a high-quality lens (device) uses multiple glass types to 'cancel out' this color-dependent bending to keep images sharp.
